name: Jesu
label: Hydra Head
lede: Justin Broadrick buried Godflesh, named the next band after its quietest song, and spent two decades making metal that sounds like a lullaby.

eras.title: Godflesh is dead
eras.text: Justin Broadrick's old band ends on a track named Jesu, and he takes the name for whatever comes next. The first songs are written and recorded largely alone, before anyone has heard a note.

years.h: [[Godflesh|864aa861-e22a-4187-8baa-2ef0c215bc0a]] close Hymns with a track called "Jesu"
years.p: The last song on the band's 2001 album is quiet and melodic, and it gives [[Justin Broadrick|d547a180-6445-42e8-96d6-aabdb6425ab1]] both a new sound and the name for his next project.
years.xp:
Wikipedia describes the track as having an unusual peacefulness and melodicism for Godflesh. Bassist and synth player [[Diarmuid Dalton|3a8877b2-c922-43fa-956f-61b240727280]], who first met Broadrick in 1984, is credited with synthesizer on Hymns.

Promotional material for the new project later carried the line "Godflesh is dead, long live Jesu."

years.h: Godflesh disband, on April 10, 2002
years.p: Wikipedia dates the split to April 10, 2002, following Justin Broadrick's nervous breakdown and Justin Green's departure the previous October.

eras.title: Two records in four months
eras.text: Jesu arrives as a 40-minute EP of two very long songs, then a full album of drone-heavy, slow, sweet songs. Ted Parsons and Diarmuid Dalton join Broadrick on record and the project becomes a band.

years.h: Heart Ache: two songs, 39 minutes, all Broadrick
years.p: Justin Broadrick plays guitar, bass, vocals and programming himself on the debut EP, released August 30, 2004 (Dry Run, per Wikipedia).

years.h: Jesu: 74 minutes on Hydra Head
years.p: The debut album, out December 8, 2004, brings in [[Ted Parsons|579dbbfe-100d-41b6-9ab7-4f7146c5d598]] on drums and [[Diarmuid Dalton|3a8877b2-c922-43fa-956f-61b240727280]] on bass for some tracks.
years.xp:
Eight tracks run 74 minutes 25 seconds. Wikipedia lists Paul Neville guesting on guitar on "Man/Woman". Pitchfork gave it 7.9. Hydra Head later pressed a 1,000-copy double vinyl picture disc in February 2005.

In 2022 Broadrick called "Tired of Me" one of his most favorite songs, saying it captured the turmoil after Godflesh ended and a major relationship breakup.

years.h: Ted Parsons and Diarmuid Dalton settle in as the rhythm section
years.p: [[Ted Parsons|579dbbfe-100d-41b6-9ab7-4f7146c5d598]], who drummed in [[Swans|3285dc48-9505-469d-ad8a-bdf2d3dba632]] and [[Prong|366b86a0-74b2-4fcb-ba79-637258299dbb]], and Dalton become Broadrick's collaborators. Dalton's Wikipedia page dates the joining to 2005.
years.xp: Parsons is a link to Broadrick's past too: Wikipedia says he played live drums for [[Godflesh|864aa861-e22a-4187-8baa-2ef0c215bc0a]] on the Songs of Love and Hate tour in 1996. Both had already played on the 2004 album, so the dates below are approximate.

years.h: Silver goes for melody and shoegaze
years.p: The four-song EP brings comparisons to My Bloody Valentine, with layered guitars where the debut had drone.

eras.title: Crossing the Atlantic
eras.text: A record cut over years arrives in 2007 with a US tour, a label showcase and a small torrent of splits. A San Francisco show in 2007 plants the seed of a longer friendship.

years.h: Conqueror trades drone for melody
years.p: Jesu's second album, out on Hydra Head in February 2007, has Broadrick, Dalton and Parsons and much more melody than the debut.

years.h: US debut opening for Isis, three weeks late
years.p: Jesu's first US shows, on the Hydra Head Records SXSW showcase and an Isis tour, were delayed by work permit trouble that cost them the tour's first three weeks.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Danny Walker was a temporary touring drummer in March 2007, with Dave Cochrane on bass. Phil Petrocelli became the touring drummer from late 2007.

Later that year the band headlined in the UK, Japan, Europe and the US.

years.h: Split 12" with Eluvium
years.p: Released July 5, 2007, the first of several Jesu splits.

years.h: Mark Kozelek sees Jesu play in San Francisco
years.p: [[Mark Kozelek|99f4b23d-3711-4efe-ad71-9572158e234c]] approached [[Justin Broadrick|d547a180-6445-42e8-96d6-aabdb6425ab1]] after a 2007 show. It leads to the 2009 EP on his label and, eventually, an album together.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Kozelek's Caldo Verde label released Jesu's Opiate Sun in 2009. In 2013 Kozelek covered a Godflesh song, and the two announced the album project in April 2015.

years.h: Pale Sketches and Lifeline arrive together
years.p: Pale Sketches comes out on Avalanche Records, Broadrick's own label; Lifeline on Hydra Head in the US and Daymare in Japan.

years.h: Splits with Envy and Battle of Mice
years.p: The Envy split came out July 11 on Daymare, the Battle of Mice split August 12 on Robotic Empire.

years.h: Why Are We Not Perfect? CDEP on Hydra Head
years.p: Released September 9, 2008. Jesu also covered Pink Floyd's "Chapter 24" for a Syd Barrett tribute and The Cure's "The Funeral Party" for a Cure tribute.

eras.title: Ascension, Broadrick alone
eras.text: The band shrinks back to Broadrick with Ted Parsons on drums. He turns toward electronics, then back to guitars, and works for years on each album.

years.h: Infinity on Avalanche
years.p: Released July 23, 2009 on Avalanche Records.

years.h: Opiate Sun on Kozelek's Caldo Verde label
years.p: The EP is Jesu's first release on the label run by [[Mark Kozelek|99f4b23d-3711-4efe-ad71-9572158e234c]] of [[Sun Kil Moon|ef2c6449-d02b-415b-ad8c-c14c08266552]].

years.h: Godflesh return, and Broadrick says Jesu drifted toward electronics
years.p: Godflesh announced a reunion in November 2009 for Hellfest 2010, and Broadrick said he would steer Jesu back to guitars, moving electronic work to Pale Sketcher.
years.xp: Hydra Head reissued Heart Ache with the unreleased 2003 EP Dethroned as Heart Ache/Dethroned on November 16, 2010. Sun Down/Sun Rise (April 23, 2007) and a Jesu/Eluvium split (July 5, 2007) are other releases from this period.

q: A downtuned Hüsker Dü or Big Star.
years.h: Ascension takes two years to write
years.p: The album was released May 10, 2011 on Caldo Verde, with Ted Parsons on drums; Broadrick played the rest at Avalanche.
years.xp: In a 2011 interview with The Obelisk, Broadrick described Jesu as pop music he loved, made heavy and melancholic, and said he spent roughly two years on Ascension. He also said the singing never comes out right on stage, which is why he prefers the studio.

years.h: Everyday I Get Closer to the Light from Which I Came
years.p: Broadrick plays everything but the strings, arranged by Nicola Manzan, on a five-song album recorded at Avalanche.

eras.title: The Sun Kil Moon years
eras.text: A friendship from a San Francisco show turns into two records with Mark Kozelek, and Broadrick closes out the decade with a new album on his own.

years.h: Jesu/Sun Kil Moon: Kozelek's songs, Broadrick's wall of guitar
years.p: [[Sun Kil Moon|ef2c6449-d02b-415b-ad8c-c14c08266552]] and Jesu released a joint album on Caldo Verde and Rough Trade on January 21, 2016, with Will Oldham, Rachel Goswell and Isaac Brock guesting.
years.xp: It was recorded in Wales and the US. Pitchfork gave it 7.5. A tour followed in February and March 2016.

years.h: A second record with Sun Kil Moon
years.p: 30 Seconds to the Decline of Planet Earth came out in May 2017.

years.h: Never in July, Terminus in November
years.p: Never is out on Bandcamp on July 3, 2020, and Terminus follows there on November 13.
